idiom_name: SeaORM entity + ActiveModel writes composed inside one transaction
implementation_notes: Rust ORMs map each table to an entity with a generated Model and ActiveModel, but none tracks a graph the way JPA does: insert the root, take the returned key, set the foreign key on every dependent ActiveModel and insert those - all inside one db transaction so the cluster commits or rolls back as one unit. SeaORM's ActiveModel is the dependable primitive (insert/update per row, on_conflict for upserts), and Diesel adds batch inserts with belonging_to inside a connection transaction. The composite boundary therefore lives in a repository function the compiler cannot check, which is why keeping the writes in one place is the whole design.
pitfalls: Without an explicit transaction each ActiveModel insert autocommits, so a failure halfway leaves the earlier dependents behind - the exact partial graph the pattern exists to prevent.
Fields left NotSet are written as NULL on update; build ActiveModels from the loaded Model rather than from defaults unless a full overwrite is intended.
SQLite and MySQL do not enforce ON DELETE CASCADE unless the migration states it, so dependents outlive the deletion of their root.
